name: Tatnuck
headline: A square where Pleasant and Chandler meet,
at the end of the old streetcar line.
answer: Tatnuck is a neighborhood on Worcester's West Side centered on Tatnuck Square, where Pleasant and Chandler Streets meet. It was a small cluster of houses by about 1830 and grew after the streetcar reached it along Pleasant Street in 1899. WRTA Route 2 still ends at Tatnuck Square, which has a city fire station, a branch library and a church, and Liberty Farm, a National Historic Landmark, stands on Mower Street.
meta: Tatnuck, Worcester: Tatnuck Square at Pleasant and Chandler Streets, the 1899 streetcar line, Liberty Farm and WRTA Route 2. A sourced West Side neighborhood guide.

boundaries.text: Tatnuck is on Worcester's West Side around Tatnuck Square, the intersection of Pleasant and Chandler Streets. West Tatnuck, which Wikipedia lists as a separate West Side neighborhood, is where the Tatnuck streetcar line was carried in 1913 and where WRTA Route 6 runs via Chandler Street.

overview: Tatnuck's name is older than the city. A Nipmuc place-name list gives 'at the great hill' as the meaning of Tatnit, listing Tatnuck as a variant spelling, and the Massachusetts Historical Commission's survey of Worcester records settlement along Tatnuck Brook in the west and suggests that a village at Tatnuck served as a gathering place before English settlement. By about 1830 the survey counts Tatnuck, at the Pleasant and Chandler Street intersection, among the small residential clusters on the edge of the town, and between 1830 and 1870 it lists Tatnuck among the places where textile mills were built on Worcester's streams.

The streetcar turned the crossroads into a square. The Worcester Consolidated Street Railway opened an extension of its Pleasant Street line to Tatnuck on May 30, 1899, pushed it 691 feet farther west in 1904, and carried it another 4,668 feet to West Tatnuck in August 1913. The route has survived as a bus: WRTA Route 2 runs to Tatnuck Square via Pleasant Street, and Route 6 runs to West Tatnuck via Chandler Street. Around the square on Pleasant Street stand the city's Tatnuck Square fire station at 1067, the First Congregational Church at 1070, where a monthly Tatnuck Square neighborhood meeting has been held, and the Worcester Public Library's Tatnuck Magnet Branch at 1083.

The neighborhood's best-known house predates the streetcar by almost a century. Liberty Farm, at 116 Mower Street, is a Federal-style farmhouse of about 1810 where the abolitionists and suffrage campaigners Abby Kelley Foster and Stephen Symonds Foster lived for most of their married life; they sheltered people escaping slavery and refused to pay property taxes because Abby could not vote. It was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1974 and remains a private residence.

housing.text: No published count of housing types or ownership for Tatnuck alone was found. The Massachusetts Historical Commission's survey records Tatnuck as one of the small residential clusters on the town's edge by about 1830, and its oldest landmark house, Liberty Farm, a c. 1810 Federal farmhouse, now stands in what its Wikipedia article calls a suburban area of western Worcester.

areas.name: Tatnuck Square
areas.line: The junction of Pleasant and Chandler Streets, the end of WRTA Route 2, with the Tatnuck Square fire station, the First Congregational Church and the Tatnuck Magnet Branch library along Pleasant Street.

areas.name: Pleasant Street
areas.line: The route the streetcar followed out to Tatnuck in 1899 and the WRTA Route 2 bus follows today.

areas.name: Mower Street
areas.line: Home of Liberty Farm at 116 Mower Street, the Foster family's c. 1810 farmhouse, which the Worcester Women's History Project places in the Tatnuck area.

commute.text: Tatnuck has no rail station; the nearest is Worcester station at Union Station, 2 Washington Square, downtown, the western end of the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line. WRTA Route 2 runs between downtown and Tatnuck Square via Pleasant Street, and Route 6 runs to West Tatnuck via Chandler Street.

places.name: Tatnuck Square
places.line: The crossroads of Pleasant and Chandler Streets, a residential cluster by about 1830 and the end of the Pleasant Street streetcar from 1899; WRTA Route 2 terminates here.

places.name: Liberty Farm
places.line: A Federal-style farmhouse of about 1810 at 116 Mower Street, home of abolitionists Abby Kelley Foster and Stephen Symonds Foster and a National Historic Landmark since 1974; it is a private residence, not open to the public.

places.name: Tatnuck Magnet Branch, Worcester Public Library
places.line: A city library branch at 1083 Pleasant Street.

places.name: First Congregational Church
places.line: A church at 1070 Pleasant Street, where the Worcester Police Department's monthly Tatnuck Square neighborhood meeting was held in 2025.

places.name: Tatnuck Square fire station
places.line: One of the city's ten fire stations, at 1067 Pleasant Street.

history.text: By about this year Tatnuck, at the Pleasant and Chandler Street intersection, had formed as one of the small residential clusters on the edge of Worcester.
The Pleasant Street streetcar line was extended to Tatnuck on May 30.
The Tatnuck line was extended 4,668 feet to West Tatnuck in August.
Liberty Farm on Mower Street was designated a National Historic Landmark on May 30.

search_notes: Exact-ranking queries for 'Tatnuck Worcester real estate' and 'moving to Tatnuck Worcester' were not run (the session's search budget ran out). Research searches for Tatnuck returned mostly individual listing pages (Pegasus Realty, RE/MAX agent sites, realty.com), Redfin neighborhood pages, a Nextdoor page and golf-course directories; Wikipedia has no Tatnuck article. A sourced guide covering the square's history, the 1899 streetcar, Liberty Farm and current bus routes has no competition.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Tatnuck, Worcester?
faq.a: The Warren Group does not report Tatnuck separately. Citywide, the median single-family sale price in Worcester for calendar year 2025 was $430,000 across 884 sales, up from $420,000 across 904 sales in 2024, according to its MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town report.

faq.q: How do you get from Tatnuck to downtown Worcester without a car?
faq.a: WRTA Route 2 runs between downtown and Tatnuck Square via Pleasant Street, following the streetcar line that reached Tatnuck in 1899, and Route 6 serves West Tatnuck via Chandler Street. Commuter rail leaves from Worcester station at Union Station, downtown, on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line.
Worcester Public Schools. School assignment is by address and is set by the district; review the district's profile with DESE.

Tatnuck Square is the intersection of Pleasant and Chandler Streets on Worcester's West Side, according to the Massachusetts Historical Commission's survey of the city. The Tatnuck Square fire station is at 1067 Pleasant Street.

faq.q: Can you visit Liberty Farm in Tatnuck?
faq.a: No. Liberty Farm, the c. 1810 home of Abby Kelley Foster and Stephen Symonds Foster at 116 Mower Street, is a National Historic Landmark but a private residence that is not open to the public.

notes: Written 2026-10-22. Tatnuck is thinly documented: Wikipedia has no Tatnuck article (the neighborhood list names Tatnuck and West Tatnuck as separate West Side neighborhoods with no boundaries), and no city neighborhood boundary or plan was found. The square's location comes from the MHC Worcester town report (Federal Period settlement pattern: 'Tatnuck (Pleasant/Chandler Street intersection)'). The MHC report also lists textile mills 'at Tatnuck' in 1830-1870 and Tatnuck Brook settlement in the Contact Period; the report's OCR text places the Tatnuck mills 'in the northeast', which conflicts with Tatnuck's West Side location, so no direction was repeated. The meaning 'at the great hill' is from the NativeTech Nipmuc place-name list (https://www.nativetech.org/Nipmuc/placenames/mainmass.html), a secondary source. Liberty Farm is placed in the 'Tatnuck Area' by the Worcester Women's History Project page; Wikipedia says only 'a suburban area of western Worcester'. The neighborhood-meeting venue is from city police calendar entries for June, August and October 2025 (nodes 47475, 47639, 47847). The fire station and library addresses are from city and library location pages. Left out for lack of a source tying them to Tatnuck: Tatnuck Country Club, Patch Reservoir, the 'Tatnuck Brook Conservation Area' (only an unsourced aggregator listing was found), Logan Field and the Tetasset Ridge/God's Acre trails on Mill Street (Wikipedia lists Mill Street as its own West Side neighborhood), Cascades Park and Coes Pond. No highway is listed because no source ties one to the neighborhood. No housing-type data for Tatnuck was found, so housing describes only the two documented facts. Market null: the Warren Group PDF lists Worcester only as a citywide row (re-read this session: 'YTD Number of Sales 904 884 -2.2%'; 'YTD Median Sale Price $420,000 $430,000 2.4%'). School assignment is by address and set by the district; the Tatnuck Magnet Branch library shares its name with a Worcester public school, which is not described or rated. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Verified the MHC report (Tatnuck at the Pleasant/Chandler Street intersection among the residential clusters by the end of the Federal period, 1775-1830; textile mills 'at Tatnuck' in the Early Industrial period, 1830-1870; Tatnuck Brook in the Contact period), the street-railway article (Pleasant Street line to Tatnuck May 30, 1899; 691 feet west on October 28, 1904; 4,668 feet to West Tatnuck in August 1913), the WRTA routes page (Route 2 Tatnuck Square via Pleasant St.; Route 6 West Tatnuck via Chandler St.), the city fire stations page (ten stations; Tatnuck Square at 1067 Pleasant Street), the library page (Tatnuck Magnet Branch, 1083 Pleasant St.), the city calendar (monthly Tatnuck Square Neighborhood Meeting at First Congregational Church, 1070 Pleasant Street, October 13, 2025), Liberty Farm on Wikipedia (116 Mower Street, c. 1810, Federal, the Fosters, sheltering people escaping slavery, tax refusal, NHL May 30, 1974, private residence, 'suburban area of western Worcester'; also on the northwestern Worcester NRHP list) and the Worcester Women's History Project ('Tatnuck Area'). Corrected: the NativeTech list has no Tatnuck entry of its own; it gives 'at the great hill' for Tatnit Hill and Brook and lists Tatnuck as a variant, and the overview now says so; the MHC report presents the Tatnuck gathering-place village as a conjecture, and the overview now says the survey 'suggests' it. Nothing removed. Fair housing: re-read; no wording describes residents.
